### Motivation
- Prevent the mobile navbar active state from revealing or animating all dropdowns at once when the nav is opened.
- Scope the active/hover visibility so each dropdown only responds to its own trigger state for predictable UX.
- Reduce reliance on a global `group-data-[state=active]` on the `#navlinks` container and move it per-dropdown.

### Description
- Removed global visibility/active classes from `#navlinks` and added `group-data-[state=active]:block` to each dropdown group in `src/components/AppHeader.astro`.

- Adjusted markup to hide mobile dropdowns by default (`hidden`/`block`) and keep each menu in its own relative container so hover/visibility and pointer-events are isolated per trigger.
- No behavioral JavaScript changes were made; this is a markup/CSS (Tailwind classes) change.

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `HOST=0.0.0.0 npm run dev -- --port 4321` and the server reported ready (success).

This pull request updates the release workflow in `.github/workflows/release.yml` to improve automation, code quality checks, and publishing steps. The most important changes include upgrading GitHub Actions dependencies, adding linting, automating artifact uploads, and enabling publishing to the VS Code Marketplace.

**Workflow improvements and automation:**

* Added `workflow_dispatch` trigger to allow manual workflow runs.
* Upgraded `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` to version 6 for better reliability and future support.
* Added an explicit lint step (`npm run lint`) to enforce code quality before releasing.
* Added a step to upload the built `.vsix` package as an artifact using `actions/upload-artifact@v4`.
* Restricted steps like version extraction, changelog extraction, release creation, and publishing to only run for tag pushes (using `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`). author: davidpmccormick
body: For #12600 ## What does this change? The `InPageNavigation` is `position: sticky` and if it opens when you are scrolled close to the bottom of the sticky container, there isn't enough room for the nav to display all of its content. This PR does two things. First it inserts a spacer element at the end of the sticky container, and gives this a height of 100vh when the menu is opened. This ensures that there will always be enough space to show the menu up to the full height of the screen. Second, it accounts for the fact that even if the menu can fill the whole screen, the items in the menu might require more than 100vh, so makes the inner `ul` scrollable. ## How to test - Turn on the twoColumns toggle - Visit the [accessibility page](https://www-dev.wellcomecollection.org/visit-us/accessibility) - Scroll near the end of the main content with a narrow and short browser (see screenshot below) - Open the nav and check that you can access all the items ## How can we measure success? The menu is accessible ## Have we considered potential risks? Can't think of any. The 100vh space is usually more space than necessary, but since it will always be enough space, I didn't think it was worth trying to work out exactly the right amount based on e.g. how far you're scrolled and how big the menu is

**why**

In last 6 months, we have experienced two times a significant slowdown in CI, that was caused by slow `setup playwright` action runs. It's a frequent call, since we use it on multiple jobs, and usual time this action takes is `1 minute` in each job (5 min or more on bad day).

We don't really need to install dependencies for OS every time on our Ubuntu boxes, we could just use cached playwright and browsers.

This setup shaves off almost a minute from playwright setup since it only uses cache now ( 5-6s instead of 1 minute on each job). Jobs seem `10-30%` faster.

Description: (https://confluentinc.atlassian.net/browse/ANSIENG-5785)

The molecule/certs-create.sh script fails to generate -key.pem files when running on systems with OpenSSL 3.x in FIPS mode (e.g., RHEL/UBI 10).

Root Cause:

On FIPS-enabled ubi10 systems (kernel fips_enabled=1), OpenSSL's FIPS provider only supports PBMAC1 for PKCS#12 MAC verification. However, Java's keytool creates PKCS#12 files using legacy PKCS12KDF, which is not FIPS-approved. When openssl pkcs12 attempts to extract keys, it fails:

Error verifying PKCS12 MAC; no PKCS12KDF support.

Impact:

Affects all molecule scenarios using custom SSL certs with fips enabled and using ubi10 image.

Solution:

Add -nomacver to bypass MAC verification in molecule/certs-create.sh.

Long-term: Wait for Java to support PBMAC1 for PKCS#12 files.

## Motivation

Some combination of Wasm target and [RPITIT](https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/return-position-impl-trait-in-trait.html) causes the compiler to ICE sometimes when invoked by `rust-analyzer`.

## Proposal

I wanted to bump the nightly and fix some new warnings.

(Note that this does not interact with https://github.com/linera-io/linera-protocol/issues/4742 because we only use the stable compiler for building applications.)

Unfortunately, our Wasmer version also has a bug that makes it incompatible with newer Rust.  We need to fix that first before actually bumping the Rust compiler.  There's nothing to stop us pre-emptively fixing the warnings though.
